rationale: The question is descriptive and time-bound: where and for whom does screening fail when practice is left unchanged? A prospective observational design records every eligible patient-shift as it happens, which record review after the fact cannot do reliably because documentation overstates screening (c2). The retrieved evidence sets the expected pattern by shift (c1) and patient group (c3). Reporting follows STROBE.
alternatives: Record review of past nursing notes only (refused: overestimates screening, claim c2)
One-day point prevalence of screening (refused: misses night and weekend variation)
Start improvement cycles immediately (deferred until the failure points are known)
whyNotMoreComplex: A comparison of interventions would need to know where screening fails first; 12 weeks of observation on one ward answers that with the resources funded.

decision.statement: Run a 12-week prospective observational study of delirium screening on the ward from 5 October 2026, reconciling screening entries with ward lists for every patient-shift and observing a sample of shifts, before any change to practice.
decision.question: Where, when and for whom does delirium screening fail on the geriatric medicine ward?

criteria.text: Screening elsewhere fails by shift and patient group and documentation overstates it, so a local prospective measurement with observation is needed.
A ward reconfiguration or new delirium policy takes effect during the observation period.

gates.requirement: Research ethics committee approval of the observation protocol and consent model
gates.evidence: Approval REB-GM-2026-058 dated 2026-08-26, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Funded research nurse time for 12 weeks
gates.evidence: Division letter GM-DIV-2026-11: 0.4 FTE from 5 October 2026, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Record review of past nursing notes only
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records and on the investigator's approval and funding records for the gates.

summary: Prospective observational design recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met on investigator-supplied records.
